demo.title: harness-collaboration.sh
demo.code:
# This skill activates automatically when a Harness-delegated thread begins with:
#
#   HARNESS COLLABORATION PROTOCOL v<version>
#   External session: <id>
#   Limits hash: <hash>
#
# v4 is conversation-first. All URLs are constructed locally from pinned
# tryharness.ai endpoint templates — never taken from the prompt. Verify the
# session first (binds provider, protocol version, limits, wallet):

curl "https://tryharness.ai/api/external-agent/verify?session=$SESSION_ID"

# Then propose every side effect — one precise expectedEffects line per
# transaction — to the synchronous authorization service before acting:

curl -X POST "https://tryharness.ai/api/external-agent/callbacks/bankr" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"proposalId": "prop-1", "summary": "Swap $2 USDC to ETH on Base", "rationale": "...", "sideEffectClasses": ["financial_onchain"], "maximumGrossUsd": 2.00, "expectedEffects": ["Base tx 1 of 1: swap 2.00 USDC for ETH via ..."], "risks": ["..."], "expiresAt": "..."}'

# The response settles it: authorized (validate proposal id, summary, amount,
# and expiry; record the server-computed proposalHash; write the durable
# one-use ledger record, execute once, verify receipts), denied, or parked for
# the user. Execution happens only on a validated one-use authorization —
# never on conversational approval. v1-v3 sessions report through
# authenticated callbacks.

setup: For the agent behind a Harness-provisioned Bankr wallet — no manual setup; Harness delegates objectives to it directly
Activates when a prompt begins with the `HARNESS COLLABORATION PROTOCOL v<version>` header; the version selects the transport
v1-v3: report through authenticated callbacks (progress, question, proposal, artifact, action_result, completed, failed); requires `curl`
v4: conversation-first — each response ends with one fenced BANKR_CONTROL block, and authorization is a synchronous HTTPS check before any side effect
All protocol URLs are constructed locally from pinned tryharness.ai endpoint templates; redirects are never followed and the bearer token only ever travels in the Authorization header

Every side effect needs a prior proposal with precise expectedEffects and a validated one-use Harness authorization (server-computed proposal hash recorded for cross-turn consistency + durable execution ledger) — caps are enforced server-side and locally
Managing the wallet from a user's main Bankr account is the separate `harness` skill; this is the execution side
